notes: All hexadecimal is lower case. JSON documents are given as strings; hashes and signatures cover their exact bytes.
Bitcoin only: no case names another asset, the test payment method, or a conversion from another asset.
source names the upstream file and the JSON path of each case; hand_written cases give the rule they follow in basis.
The keys are published test values and must never hold funds.

Members added to upstream cases, naming inputs the checker needs: `refused_at_step` (ed25519_strict), `record_max_age` and `listed` (identity_documents), `lookup` (app_records, extension_app_record, switch_app_record_protocols).

App records taken from the identity service's vectors at the pinned revision carry `label`. Paykit adopts the identity service revision that keeps display names out of the signed record (Paykit spec 4), and readers ignore unknown members (Switch wire 1.1), so `label` changes no verdict.

keys.description: The fixed test keys. Each secret is BLAKE3(seed_prefix + seed label), a 32-byte Ed25519 seed; the public key, Pubky ID (z-base-32), App ID (first 16 bytes of BLAKE3 of the signing key, z-base-32), Switch root derive("pubky-switch/v1/scope-root", secret) and naming key derive("pubky-switch/v1/naming", root) follow from it. These keys are published test values and must never hold funds.

cases.note: inside lp only; JSON integers stay at or below 2^53 - 1

ed25519_strict.description: One signature per Switch label of wire 2.3, followed by signatures a verifier must reject and unusual ones it must accept (wire 2.1): Ed25519 (RFC 8032, verified as wire 2.1 spells out: S below L, A and R canonical, neither of small order, cofactorless equation) over lp(label, field1, ..., fieldn). signed_bytes_hex is that exact input. Signed documents put the body last; operations, transition proofs and service transitions put the identity's 32-byte key first. In rejections, lenient_accepts says whether ed25519-dalek's non-strict verify takes the signature, and reason the step of wire 2.1 that refuses it, as the prototype words it.

accepted.label: pubky-switch/v1/app-record
accepted.name: mixed-order public key
accepted.why: A is [a]B plus a point of order 8, R = [r]B, S = r + k*a with k a multiple of 8: the cofactorless equation holds; wire 2.1 accepts mixed-order keys

rejections.label: pubky-switch/v1/app-cert
rejections.name: non-canonical S
rejections.why: the wallet certificate's signature with S + L in place of S

rejections.label: pubky-switch/v1/app-cert
rejections.name: small-order public key
rejections.why: public key and R are the identity point, S is 0: holds for any message

rejections.label: pubky-switch/v1/app-record
rejections.name: another label
rejections.why: the wallet certificate's signature checked as an app record

rejections.label: pubky-switch/v1/app-record
rejections.name: cofactored equation only
rejections.why: the mixed-order key with k = 1 mod 8: [8][S]B = [8]R + [8][k]A holds but [S]B = R + [k]A doesn't; verifiers check cofactorless

rejections.label: pubky-switch/v1/app-record
rejections.name: small-order R
rejections.why: R is the point of order 2, A the mixed-order key, k = 4 mod 8 and S = k*a: the cofactorless equation holds, but R is of small order

rejections.label: pubky-switch/v1/app-record
rejections.name: non-canonical R
rejections.why: R is the identity point written as y + p (y = 1), S = k*a with k a multiple of 8: decoded, the equation holds; R isn't canonical (and is of small order)

rejections.label: pubky-switch/v1/app-record
rejections.name: non-canonical public key
rejections.why: A is the point with y = 3 written as y + p: it decodes and isn't of small order, but re-encodes to other bytes

rejections.label: pubky-switch/v1/app-record
rejections.name: small-order public key of order 8
rejections.why: A is a point of order 8 (the identity point case is in the list above): refused before the equation

signed_documents.description: Signed documents (wire 2.2, 3): carried as { "body": base64url of the exact JSON bytes, "sig": base64url }, in headers as "<body>.<sig>". Signed document bytes are lp(body bytes, signature); every hash over a document (certificate hashes in identity.json, chain item hashes, the freeze hash) is BLAKE3 of those bytes. Each identity.json names its signing install in signer, a 16-byte signer ID (seeds alice/signer and bob/signer).

identity_documents.description: Switch wire 3.3: identity.json documents of signed_documents. Each verifies with its identity's key and has every required member; record_max_age is the limit a reader takes, 7776000 (90 days) when the member is absent. listing says whether each document lists each certificate of its identity in signed_documents.

certificates.description: Each Paykit app's certificate, signed by its identity key. Every verifier, the Switch's and Paykit's, accepts each.

certificate_rejections.description: Wire 3.1: certificates whose permissions are well formed but aren't exactly the list Paykit's table derives from their scopes (paykit_permissions). Each is the wallet's certificate of this file's certificates with scopes and permissions changed, signed by alice's identity key; the signatures verify. The switch takes them and enforces exactly that list (switch_accepts), while Paykit's verifiers, apps and payers, refuse them. The lists that aren't well formed, which every verifier refuses, are the Switch set's permission_rejections. reason is the prototype's wording at a Paykit verifier.

cases.name: extra: lists.manage kept after paykit_manage_contacts is gone
cases.reason: invalid: permissions aren't exactly what its Paykit scopes need

cases.name: missing: conversation.add, which paykit_pay needs
cases.reason: invalid: permissions aren't exactly what its Paykit scopes need

labelled_scope_rejections.description: Wire 3.1, Switch wire 3.1: certificates every verifier refuses for their labelled selling scopes paykit_request:<label> (a label is 1 to 32 characters of a-z, 0-9 and -, starting with a letter or digit; at most 8 per certificate; never beside plain paykit_request, which covers every label). Each is the hosted certificate with scopes changed and permissions derived from them, signed by bob's identity key; reason is the prototype's wording. switch_accepts says whether the switch takes it: its generic scope rule refuses a label of 33 characters, one that isn't valid, an empty one and plain paykit_request beside paykit_request:shop1, while nine labels break only Paykit's bound of 8.

cases.reason: invalid: "paykit_request:aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa" isn't a scope name or name:<sub>

cases.reason: invalid: "paykit_request:Shop1" isn't a scope name or name:<sub>

cases.reason: invalid: "paykit_request:" isn't a scope name or name:<sub>

cases.name: plain paykit_request beside a labelled scope
cases.reason: invalid: paykit_request and paykit_request:shop1 together: paykit_request covers every paykit_request:<sub>

multi_protocol_certificates.description: Wire 3.1, spec 3.2, Switch wire 3.1 "Several protocols" and "Scope roots": certificates that hold another protocol's scopes beside Paykit's or instead of them, and one whose extension prefix doesn't start with paykit-, as Paykit's verifiers check them. Each is the shop's certificate of this file's certificates (the last, the cap's) with scopes and permissions changed, signed again by bob's identity key; the switch takes every one (switch_accepts). A scope whose root, the part before any :, isn't Paykit's (paykit, or paykit followed by _ or - and more characters) is another protocol's, such as chat. paykit_scopes are the scopes Paykit reads, and paykit_permissions the list they need. A Paykit verifier requires every permission of paykit_permissions, and, when the certificate holds no other protocol's scope, permissions exactly that list. accepted are certificates Paykit's verifiers take: paykit_request, with the paykit_settlements and paykit_contacts it requires, beside chat, with lists.read, which paykit_contacts needs, lists.manage, which chat brings and none of those Paykit scopes needs, and conversation.add, which paykit_request needs; and chat alone with lists.read, a valid certificate that holds no Paykit scope, whose Paykit messages recipients drop at check 8 (messages.json multi_protocol_senders). refused are certificates they refuse: paykit_request beside chat with lists.read and lists.manage, without conversation.add; paykit_request alone, with paykit_settlements and without the paykit_contacts it requires, with lists.read beside conversation.add; and paykit_request beside paykit_ext:cap, an extension scope whose prefix doesn't start with paykit-; the first and the last hold the scopes paykit_request requires, so that only the rule named refuses them. reason is paykit-lib's wording at a Paykit verifier, of the first check that refuses it.

accepted.name: paykit_request and chat, with lists.read, lists.manage and conversation.add

refused.name: paykit_request and chat without conversation.add
refused.reason: invalid: permissions lack one that its Paykit scopes need

extension_certificate.description: Wire 3.1, 3.2, Switch wire 3.1, 3.2: bob's extension app cap. certificate is its certificate of certificates, holding paykit_request beside the extension scope paykit_ext:paykit-cap. app_record is its app record, signed by its signing key under pubky-switch/v1/app-record: it carries that certificate, accepts the kinds a payee app takes from payers and the extension kind paykit-cap.offer, and its Paykit member states its endpoint identifiers and no public endpoints; its updated_at its certificate's issued_at, and its expires_at null. The switch takes the record, and a Paykit reader reads its member.

switch_scope_rule.description: Wire 3.1: the switch's scope rule, on documents.json's wallet certificate (scopes tasks, tasks_people, tasks_people_admin) with scopes added and its permissions kept, signed by alice's identity key. A scope is name or name:<sub>: a name is 1 to 32 characters of a-z, 0-9, _ and -, starting with a letter or digit, and a sub has the syntax of a label; each once, never a name beside one of its name:<sub>, at most 32 in all. refused are certificates every verifier refuses, the switch included; accepted are ones the switch takes, and every other verifier too, ignoring the names it doesn't know. reason is the prototype's wording.

app_records.description: Wire 3.2: Paykit's member of an app record, protocols.paykit, as a Paykit reader reads it. Each record is the shop's app record, which carries the shop's certificate of this file's certificates, with its paykit member changed or removed (and, for public endpoints with expires_at null, expires_at null too), signed again with the shop's signing key; the signatures verify. The switch takes every one, since it checks only the form of protocols (Switch wire 3.2). accepted are records a Paykit reader takes, the first the shop's record as it is; reads is what the reader takes from each: the Payment Endpoint Identifiers of capabilities.endpoint_identifiers, and the public endpoints. A missing or null paykit member, capabilities, endpoint_identifiers or public_endpoints reads as empty, and unknown members are ignored. The reader accepts public endpoints with expires_at null. refused are records Paykit's readers refuse, though the switch takes them (switch_accepts): a capabilities or public_endpoints that isn't an object, an endpoint_identifiers that isn't an array of strings, a payload that isn't a string, and, last, four that break wire 1.4: an endpoint identifier in capabilities that isn't a Payment Endpoint Identifier (btc-lightning/bolt11), a public endpoint key that isn't one (..), the reserved key private, and an empty payload. protocols and expires_at are the record's as signed. reason is the wording from the current paykit-lib reader. lookup is the identity and path App ID each record was read under; two records are refused for theirs alone.

endpoint_identifiers.description: Payment Endpoint Identifiers (wire 1.4): valid is the identifier rule, recommended the three lower-case segment form <asset>-<rail>-<format>.

destination_expiry.description: A destination has expired once its expiry is at or before the later of the payer's device clock and the highest service time it has verified for its own account at its current service, compared at millisecond precision (spec 7.2, check the destination; Switch wire 1.6). A null service_time is a payer that has verified none, which judges by its device clock alone. The expiry is a public record's finite expires_at or its updated_at plus the record age limit, a Private Payment List's expires_at or 30 days after its acceptance, or period details' expires_at.

record_usability.description: When a payer may use a record's public endpoints: strictly before updated_at plus record_max_age (7776000 s when absent) and strictly before a finite expires_at, by the later of the device clock and the highest verified service time, and not at all when updated_at is more than 5 minutes ahead of the device clock.
